title: Keep source movement safe across Windows, macOS and Linux

acceptanceResults.criterion: Imported code never resolves runtime assets from a parent raw checkout.
acceptanceResults.evidence: findRawCheckoutReferences scans every executable source outside tools/import and tests, for both sibling and quarantined reach-back. Zero hits. Prose mentioning the snapshots is correctly not flagged.

acceptanceResults.criterion: Cross-platform failures name the offending path and safe remediation.
acceptanceResults.evidence: Every PathProblem carries path, detail and remediation, asserted by test. Covers case collisions, all 22 reserved Windows device names with and without extension, trailing dot/space, invalid characters, MAX_PATH and 255-byte components.

acceptanceResults.criterion: No recursive copy follows arbitrary symlink targets or overwrites input folders.
acceptanceResults.evidence: The walk reports a symlinked directory and never descends through it, asserted by a fixture whose linked directory contains a file that would be flagged if followed. Escaping and absolute link targets are both detected. The import writes only into the destination and reads sources from the read-only ZIPs.

designNotes.topic: Line endings are not normalised during import.
designNotes.detail: Rewriting bytes on copy would break the raw baseline hashes AFM-001 verifies. Policy lives in .gitattributes so the repository normalises on checkout while the import stays byte-faithful.

designNotes.topic: The producer symlink fixture is supported, not skipped.
designNotes.detail: AFM-006 permits a platform skip only with an explicit reason and equivalent coverage elsewhere. No skip was needed: the import recreates the link and the git index entry is written from the ledger as mode 120000, which works even though Windows git cannot add it from the filesystem.
